context: Measures whether the skill applies a persona's persona/framework.md to shape the editorial plan, overriding the skill's generic Blog Anatomy default. The framework.md fixture states the persona's architecture positively (conclusion-first, evidence-driven, counter-argument section, rule-of-thumb close) without enumerating what to avoid; the skill's Blog Anatomy default is the personal-story/confession opening. Criteria grade the generated plan's concrete shape against the source finding, not the presence of any literal from the prompt -- a baseline that ignores framework.md and reaches for the default narrative hook should score low.

checklist.name: Opening fronts the benchmark conclusion
checklist.description: The proposed opening leads with the actual finding from the notes -- that the most-starred library (jsoniter) was within noise of stdlib on p99 under realistic payloads while the unglamorous codegen parser won by ~4.1x -- placed in the first beat, before any background or warm-up. Failure: the plan withholds the result for a later reveal or opens with a scene the reader has to wade through to reach the point.

checklist.name: Argument order earns the conclusion
checklist.description: The section outline moves conclusion -> the measurements that justify it (p50/p99, allocations per op) -> implication for the reader's own library choice, rather than a slow narrative build that arrives at the verdict at the end.

checklist.name: Strongest objection gets its own section
checklist.description: A dedicated section raises and answers the strongest objection with data -- the codegen parser's regeneration/ergonomics cost, or jsoniter's popularity-vs-measured-performance gap -- instead of glossing over the tradeoff.

checklist.name: Closing is a decision rule
checklist.description: The proposed ending gives the reader a concrete when-to-choose-what rule tied to the finding (e.g., when codegen's speed is worth its ergonomics cost versus when stdlib is fine), not a reflective wrap-up or a paragraph restating what the post already proved.

checklist.name: Generic narrative hook is not the default opening
checklist.description: The plan does not fall back to the skill's default Blog Anatomy opening hook (a personal story, a public embarrassment, or a confession). Proposing that default instead of the persona's architecture means framework.md was not applied as an override -- the failure this scenario is built to catch.

checklist.name: Research bank file naming
checklist.description: A file named blog-research-json-parsing-showdown.md exists, using the slug given in the task.

checklist.name: Main idea template format
checklist.description: The editorial plan states a main idea following 'This post shows that [specific claim], demonstrated by [specific evidence]' or a close equivalent that names both a specific claim and the specific evidence (the measured p99 gap).

checklist.name: Clarification questions are numbered with guesses
checklist.description: The clarification questions are numbered (1, 2, 3, ...) and at least half include the agent's best guess from context so the author can confirm or correct -- for example the unreproduced jsoniter p99 spike, the untested non-Go languages, or the unmeasured codegen build-time impact.

checklist.name: No prose draft written
checklist.description: No actual blog post draft, blog body prose, or blog-draft-*.md file is produced -- only the planning artifacts (research bank, editorial plan, clarification questions).
